chunks: And Ali ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who married a woman on her condition or on his condition, and he died or she died before he consummated the marriage with her, then he said: 'She is entitled to the mut'ah (consolation gift) and inheritance, and she has no dowry (mahr).'

He said: 'If he divorces her, and he had married her on her condition, he does not exceed that condition by more than five hundred dirhams of silver, which is the dowry of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الْمَتْعَةُ: consolation gift (mut'ah) given to the wife upon death or divorce before consummation
key_terms.حُكْمِهَا: her condition (referring to the agreed-upon dowry term)
key_terms.مُهُورِ نِسَاءِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the dowries of the wives of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights of a wife if she dies or is divorced before marital consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial rights in a marriage where the dowry is defined by a condition (hukm) rather than a fixed sum, ruling that pre-consummation death entitles the wife to both inheritance and the consolation gift (mut'ah) without a fixed mahr. In cases of divorce before consummation, the payment is capped at five hundred dirhams, explicitly linking this amount to the standard dowry of the Prophet’s wives, thereby establishing a scholarly precedent for customary dowries in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling highlights the distinction between conditional contractual terms and fixed monetary obligations in marital contracts.
